nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real vector space, let $s \subseteq E$ be convex, and let $(g_i)_{i \in t}$ be a finite family of functions $E \to \mathbb{R}$, each convex on $s$. Then $x \mapsto \sum_{i \in t} g_i(x)$ is convex on $s$; for $t = \emptyset$ it is the constant $0$. Lagrangians, empirical risks and regularized losses are convex by this rule.
nodes.title: Finite sums of convex functions are convex

nodes.summary: Let $E$ be a real Banach space, let $X \subseteq E$ be an open convex set, and let $f \colon E \to \mathbb{R}$ be twice continuously differentiable on $X$. Then $f$ is convex on $X$ if and only if $f(x) \ge f(a) + Df(a)(x - a)$ for all $a, x \in X$, where $Df(a)$ is the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $a$ within $X$.

nodes.summary: A differentiable function is convex exactly when each of its first-order Taylor approximations is a global underestimator, $f(x) \ge f(a) + Df(a)(x - a)$.
